title: Duel balance patch — changes only
summary: Your reviewed patch with four rebalanced catch-up designs, based on current Duel card comparisons and explicit value calculations. Aegis remains unchanged from the previous proposal because its conditional fast-play already refunds its cost. Only changed or new game content is listed. The full patch still awaits gameplay implementation and testing.

cohort.format: Duel, Nyou Haïai with search on both sides
cohort.matchups: 189 games in each of the 20 ordered matchups of different heroes; no mirrors
cohort.validation_plan: After the review, define the intended package and its acceptable balance range. Compare baseline, individual changes and their combination on paired seeds with both starting seats. Track hero matchups, relic choices and rewards, opening-card availability, victory routes and game-length tails. Give the policy an opportunity to adapt before treating the result as final balance; self-play's aggregate win rate is always 50% and is not a patch success metric.

proposals.title: Giga: Dominion mastery 3 → 2
proposals.confidence: Strong imbalance signal; moderate confidence in this tuning
proposals.current: Cost 2, defense 4. When played, draw 1 card. Exhaust — Dominion: gain 3 mastery.
proposals.proposed: In Duel only, change the Dominion exhaust to gain 2 mastery. Keep cost 2, defense 4 and the draw on play. Add a Duel replacement so the original card remains unchanged in other formats.
proposals.reason: Reduce a cheap champion's repeated mastery acceleration while preserving its identity and accessibility. This is the strongest opening outlier supported by both acquisition and initial-market evidence. A normal purchase puts Giga into discard; the draw is on playing it, not on buying it.
evidence: Giga was in the initial market in 117 games. The first player acquired it in all 117 and won 82, or 70.1%; first-player wins were 51.1% when Giga was absent.
The initial-offer association remains about +18.1 percentage points after controlling hero matchup and both opening hands' buying power; the 95% interval is +9.4 to +26.8 points.
Players acquiring Giga by round 2 won 145/206 games, or 70.4%. Successful Dominion triggers were not logged, so the exact contribution of each activation remains unknown.

interactions.text: These Dominion reductions stack in early Order decks.
Omnius also produces less Dominion mastery.
The cheaper Abstractor gives a different early mastery route.

watch: Initial-market Giga advantage and early purchase rate
Successful Dominion triggers and mastery 10/20/30 timing
Rez's matchups and the overall share of mastery victories
Round distribution, including unusually early finishes

response.explanation: Retained the accepted change and applied your latest wording requests.

proposals.title: Deadly Recruits: activation costs 1 gem
proposals.confidence: Strong selection signal; moderate confidence in the amount
proposals.current: Exhaust for no gem cost: choose an ally in the market costing 2 or less, then fast-play it OR recruit it for free. At mastery 20, the limit becomes 4.
proposals.proposed: Pay 1 gem and exhaust, then fast-play OR recruit one eligible ally. Remove “for free” from the card text. Eligibility remains cost 2 or less, upgraded to 4 or less at M20. The chosen card has no additional purchase payment; the 1 gem is the activation cost.
proposals.reason: Charge for repeatable access to immediate effects or permanent cards. Reducing only recruitment would miss the principal observed use, which is fast-play. One gem could be too severe for an already conditional market-dependent action, so its choice and usage rates matter.
evidence: Normal selectors won 64.5% of 752 games. The association remains about +11.0 percentage points after matchup, seat and selection-timing adjustment.
Of 3,043 recorded mode choices, 2,554 were fast-play and 489 recruit: approximately 84% fast-play.
The favorable raw result appears across all five heroes, although choosing the destiny remains a strategic, nonrandom event.

interactions.text: Cost-2 Abstractor becomes an early eligible target.
Aegis can refund the activation gem if its mastery condition succeeds.
The new cost-2 Scout is an eligible fast-play target before M20.

watch: Choice rate when this destiny is available
Paid activations, eligible targets and successful fast-play/recruit resolutions
Pre-mastery-20 usefulness versus other destinies

proposals.title: Multitask Brain: pre-mastery-20 power per faction 2 → 1
proposals.confidence: Strong Tetra signal; moderate confidence in the relic attribution
proposals.current: For each distinct faction played this turn, gain 2 power and draw 1 card. At mastery 20, gain 4 power per faction instead. The faction count is evaluated before these draws.
proposals.proposed: Below mastery 20, gain 1 power and draw 1 card per distinct faction played. At mastery 20, retain 4 power and 1 draw per faction. Keep Tetra's hero power unchanged.
proposals.reason: Reduce the damage attached to Tetra's exceptionally strong draw engine without removing her cycling identity. This halves the relic's early power, a substantial change; retaining the mastery-20 reward gives the build a later payoff.
evidence: Tetra wins 876/1,512 games, or 57.9%, and leads against every opposing hero. Ordinary damage accounts for 77.7% of her wins.

Brain is 90.1% of Tetra's normal relic choices; those games win 734/1,190, or 61.7%. The timing-adjusted association is similar, but hero power, relic choice and deck quality are not causally separated.

A normal Brain play supplies its own Order faction. Prism can supply all five factions, giving the current card a maximum of 10 power plus 5 draws below mastery 20. The proposal lowers that maximum to 5 power plus 5 draws; mastery-20 output stays 20 power plus 5 draws.

interactions.text: Lower early Tetra damage and Crown’s improved cycling can strengthen Volos together.

watch: Every Tetra matchup and both starting seats
Brain output per faction, tier and play
Switching to other relics
Late mastery wins, long games and the size of the mastery-20 power jump

proposals.title: Panconscious Crown: add Draw 1
proposals.confidence: Strong route weakness; uncertain rules-versus-policy cause
proposals.current: Gain 2 mastery and 5 health. Then, at mastery 20, Unify grants another 50 health. Crown's own mastery gain can reach the threshold before the check.
proposals.proposed: Gain 2 mastery, 5 health and draw a card. Then check M20 Unify to gain 50 health. Resolve mastery, healing, draw, then the M20 Unify check in that order, as you confirmed. The newly drawn card may be revealed to satisfy Unify; Crown’s own mastery gain can reach M20.
proposals.reason: Improve Crown’s cycling. You requested one combined base-effect line and confirmed that the draw happens before the M20 Unify check. This is an explicit timing change from the previous draw-last draft.
evidence: Crown selectors win 95/299 games, or 31.8%, versus 485/998, or 48.6%, for Talons. The large gap persists after measured selection and mastery timing adjustment.
Crown players reach mastery 20 in 59.5% of games, yet average 10.96 rounds and frequently fail to finish. Volos already reaches mastery 10 most often, so earlier access is not the obvious bottleneck.

Volos acquired both Crown and Talons in 75 games and won 60, or 80.0%. These selected reward-enriched decks do not establish a causal combo win rate. Mechanically, Talons before Crown can convert Crown's 5 + 50 healing into 55 power, even at full health.

interactions.text: Volos also gets +1 power on his paid power mode.
The new conditional healing can also interact with Volos’s healing-to-power relic.

Same-turn relic order and healing converted to power, including at full health

proposals.title: New card · Horizon Seeker
proposals.confidence: Calculated design revision using effective Duel peers. Exact balance and trigger frequencies require future gameplay validation.
proposals.current: New card; no current version.
proposals.proposed: Cost 2, Order ally, 2 copies. Draw a card, then if your mastery is lower than your opponent’s, gain 2 mastery. The conditional bonus increases from 1 to 2. Ties give no bonus; check after the draw. A one-point deficit may become a one-point lead, which switches off later catch-up bonuses.
proposals.reason: The original one-mastery reward was too small for a card whose entire resource output switches off at parity. The revised conditional reward gives a useful catch-up play while the tied/ahead version remains only a cantrip.
evidence: Cloud Oracles costs 2, draws 1, and gives 2 gems when ahead in mastery. Revised Shard Seer costs 2 and draws 1 with 1 mastery on an Infinity Shard reveal. Cache Warden costs 2 for 1 mastery and draws at M10.

At an assumed 50% chance of being behind on resolution, average mastery per play rises from 0.5 to 1.0. At 0% it remains 0; at 100% it rises from 1 to 2. These are sensitivity inputs, not measured trigger rates.
Playing the owned card spends one hand card and draws one replacement: net hand count 0 before any other effect. Its draw is not a free extra card on top of an intact hand.

interactions.text: Same cost and draw baseline; Seeker gains 2 mastery only while behind, while revised Shard Seer gains 1 on its reveal condition.

watch: Availability and fast-play frequency while behind versus ahead in mastery.
Copy, free-play and faction-combination interactions across the whole package.

response.comment:
rework the catchup cards and make one for every faction. Instead of different "if you have less X than your opponent", only use "if you have less mastery than your opponent". mastery check only. Then the bonuses can vary:
order: if less mastery, gain mastery
wraethe: if less mastery, banish a card
undergrowth: if less mastery, heal
homodeus: if less mastery, gain cristals
aion: if less mastery, warp
response.explanation: Reassessed after your request for better balance and value calculations. Revised the exact numbers; your mastery-only condition, faction role and two-copy quantity remain.

design_notes: Keep the condition strict and evaluate each copy separately. The larger bonus can erase the deficit; later copies cannot reuse the earlier state.
This remains an ally: it cannot be paid-fast-played directly. It can be reached by eligible Warp and Deadly Recruits effects.
Do not convert mastery into a fixed gem value: focus is once per turn and mastery thresholds can change the value sharply.

proposals.title: New card · Riftbreaker
proposals.confidence: Calculated design revision using effective Duel peers. Exact balance and trigger frequencies require future gameplay validation.
proposals.current: New card; no current version.
proposals.proposed: Cost 2 → 3 and base power 3 → 5. Keep the optional banish of one card from hand or discard while behind in mastery. Wraethe mercenary, 2 copies. It now has a useful attack floor even without the banish, at a higher purchase and paid-fast-play cost.
proposals.reason: The old card gained only one power over Shadow Apostle while losing reliable banishing, and had less power than Nil Assassin. A five-power cost-3 mercenary creates a separate combat option; putting four power plus a conditional banish at cost 2 would simply outclass Nil Assassin’s printed output.
evidence: Effective Duel Nil Assassin: cost 2 mercenary, 4 power. Shadow Apostle: cost 2 mercenary, 2 power plus an unconditional optional banish. The proposed cost-3 Riftbreaker pays one extra gem for 3 extra power over Apostle, with a less reliable banish.

Same-cost Le’shai Knight gives 4 power or 6 with Unify; Riftbreaker’s unconditional 5 sits between those amounts. The Lost costs 4 for 5 power and an Allegiance-gated banish, which can keep working while ahead in mastery.
Paid fast-play power per gem rises from 3/2 = 1.50 to 5/3 = 1.67. This ratio describes immediate power only; it does not price the banish or future owned plays.
At an assumed 50% mastery-trigger rate, either design offers 0.5 optional banish opportunities per play. The improvement is its power output, not a fictitious increase in banish reliability.

interactions.text: J-Chord’s Warp 3 can reach this cost-3 mercenary.
Riftbreaker requires the M20 cost-4 tier; it no longer qualifies for the early cost-2 tier.

watch: Availability and fast-play frequency while behind versus ahead in mastery.
Copy, free-play and faction-combination interactions across the whole package.

response.comment:
rework the catchup cards and make one for every faction. Instead of different "if you have less X than your opponent", only use "if you have less mastery than your opponent". mastery check only. Then the bonuses can vary:
order: if less mastery, gain mastery
wraethe: if less mastery, banish a card
undergrowth: if less mastery, heal
homodeus: if less mastery, gain cristals
aion: if less mastery, warp
response.explanation: Reassessed after your request for better balance and value calculations. Revised the exact numbers; your mastery-only condition, faction role and two-copy quantity remain.

design_notes: Cost 3 keeps it outside Warp 2, pre-M20 Deadly Recruits and the cost-2 Conscription condition. J-Chord’s Warp 3 and M20 Deadly Recruits still reach it.

One banish has no fixed gem value. Example: with 8 useful cards in a 20-card deck, banishing one other card raises expected useful cards in a five-card hand from 2.000 to 2.105. Future cycles and the removed card’s value determine the benefit.
Compare it in attack decks with Nil Assassin and Le’shai Knight, and in thinning decks with Shadow Apostle. The goal is a reason to choose each, rather than an unconditional replacement.

proposals.confidence: Calculated design revision using effective Duel peers. Exact balance and trigger frequencies require future gameplay validation.
proposals.current: New card; no current version.

proposals.title: New card · Rift Scout
proposals.confidence: Calculated design revision using effective Duel peers. Exact balance and trigger frequencies require future gameplay validation.
proposals.current: New card; no current version.
proposals.proposed: Keep cost 2 and 3 power; raise the conditional Warp limit from 1 to 2. Aion ally, 2 copies. Only lower mastery enables Warp, and a legal target must still be present. The higher limit addresses the bonus’s second failure condition: lack of eligible targets.
proposals.reason: Warp 1 had too few legal targets to be a dependable catch-up reward. The previous card also lost power, shield and unconditional activation versus Brute. Warp 2 repairs the target shortage while retaining those meaningful differences.
evidence: Brute costs 3 for 4 power, Shield 2 and unconditional Warp 2. Revised Scout costs one less but has 1 less power, no shield and a mastery condition. Brute retains substantial advantages.

The revised full Duel stock contains 184 physical row cards, including ten new copies. Warp 1 reaches 16 copies; Warp 2 reaches 64. For a random six, P(at least one target) = 1 − C(N−K,6)/C(N,6): 42.52% versus 92.64%.

For a later random row after owning one Scout, exclude that copy: N=183, with 16 Warp-1 targets or 63 Warp-2 targets. Availability is 42.71% versus 92.39%. These are fresh-stock examples, not observed match statistics.
At an illustrative 50% chance of being behind and that row model, a legal Warp opportunity rises from 0.214 to 0.462 per play. A legal target is not necessarily a valuable target.

proposals.title: Champion attacks: choose their timing and order
proposals.confidence: Requested or accepted in your review; combined balance impact remains untested.
proposals.current:
Power attacks against champions are assigned together at the end of the turn.
Testudo shield reactions are also deferred.
proposals.proposed: Spend power on a champion attack during your turn, between playing cards, recruiting and using abilities. Commit the target and power, resolve any permitted shields, damage and destruction immediately, then choose your next action. Zetta must actually leave play before its owner or other protected champions become legal targets. Remaining power attacks players together at turn end. There is no second unordered champion split at the end.
proposals.reason: This restores the official attack timing and makes removal order meaningful. Testudo, shield budgets and aura-damage timing require explicit local rules; those recommendations are shown below and in Testudo’s separate proposal.
evidence: The publisher’s Saga rulebook, page 13, permits champion attacks during the turn and places player damage at turn end. It normally excludes shields from champion defense.

Zetta’s printed protection concerns attacks. Treating direct destruction as separate follows that wording, the official Li Hin/Thorn Zealot distinction and the current local engine; no Zetta-specific destruction FAQ was found.

interactions.text: Review the proposed per-champion shield allowance and its Zetta interaction.

watch: Zetta plus Testudo: if Zetta survives shield prevention, the other targets remain protected; if it dies, recalculate legal targets immediately.
Attacks spend committed power even if prevented. Overkill does not spill into player damage, and shield reveals do not permit undoing the attack.
Recheck Li Hin, Raidian, Drakonarius and all other attack restrictions after every action.
After aura removal, recompute effective defense and remove champions with lethal marked damage, repeating until stable. Prevention already applied is never undone.
Both Auld Haïai and Nyou Haïai, training legal actions, snapshots, saves and reconnects must understand the new attack and shield state before new games are evaluated.

response.comment: We can kill champions during the turn and in the order we want.
response.explanation: Your requested timing is included. The local interaction details remain recommendations for your review.

sources.title: Official Saga rulebook · attacks and shields, page 13

design_notes: Recommended declaration rule: assign at least the champion’s remaining effective defense before shields; extra power may be committed to overcome protection. If shields prevent a kill, damage persists until this turn ends and a later attack may finish it. The official book does not explicitly settle arbitrary partial declarations; this minimum is a proposed clarification, not a claimed official FAQ ruling.

Zetta plus Testudo: attack Zetta first and finish its shield decision. If Zetta survives, no other protected target is unlocked. Direct destroy effects can remove Testudo first because they are not attacks.
When a defense aura leaves play, recompute live defense and destroy already-lethal champions until stable. Resolve simultaneous removals as a batch so collection order cannot decide survival.

If a future card permits several Zettas, a possible explicit house rule is that guards protect non-guards and their owner but not one another. Do not silently add that rule or alter Zetta now; the current deck has only one.

Offer an Attack for N button based on public remaining defense, plus a power amount for shield overpayment. Only publicly revealed shields inform hints. Resolve one defense prompt at a time and return control after all consequences.
At end turn, allocate remaining power to players only. If all opposing players are protected by Zetta, blocked power expires; never force an impossible assignment.

proposals.title: Testudo Vanguard: shields across ordered attacks
proposals.confidence: Custom champion timing recommendation; not an official Testudo rule and not yet approved or tested.
proposals.current:
Your shields are also applied to each of your champions individually.
Exhaust: gain 2 gems.
proposals.proposed: Keep cost 4, defense 4 and Exhaust: gain 2 gems. While Testudo is in play, each of your champions, including Testudo, has its own allowance from each shield source for the current opponent’s turn. Repeated attacks consume that champion’s remaining allowance; they never refresh it. The player keeps a separate allowance for the final player attack. If the last Testudo dies, later champion attacks receive no shield protection.
proposals.reason: Preserves Testudo’s existing protection for each champion without granting unlimited prevention from repeated attacks. Spending one pool across the whole army would instead be a substantial additional nerf, so separate allowances are recommended.

interactions.text: Zetta protection and live aura changes resolve between these attacks.
Hermit gains a new Shield 2 source for this interaction.

watch: A 4-power hit on defense-4 Testudo against Shield 3 leaves 1 damage. A later 3-power hit kills it unless another unused shield is revealed; the same Shield 3 cannot recharge.
Destroying Testudo disables subsequent champion protection but does not undo earlier prevention or consume the player’s separate shield allowance.
Two copies of a shield each contribute. Two Testudos do not multiply or reset the protection.
Ru Bo Vai ignores shields for later attacks only; it does not undo previously prevented damage.

response.comment: Suggest good ways to handle those special champions.
response.explanation: This is the recommended adaptation of the custom Testudo ability to your requested combat timing. Review these rules before gameplay implementation.

design_notes: The attacker commits power before the defender decides whether to reveal eligible hand shields. Revealed cards stay in hand; each physical card establishes its own reveal-time allowance per protected champion and separately for the player. Use actual prevented damage to consume allowance, carrying unused prevention through this opponent’s turn.

Previously revealed allowances apply automatically. The defender can reveal additional unused hand shields on a later attack, but cannot undo damage already dealt. Revealing the same instance again never resets its usage.

A hand shield’s revealed allowance lasts for the rest of that attacking turn even if that card later leaves hand. This is an explicit proposed duration for the custom mechanic. Champion use still requires a live Testudo.

Passive shields, including Praetorian-02 in play and eligible Datic Robes in discard, are accounted for per physical source and per target. Unused passive protection requires its source and condition to remain active. Source removal or zone cycling never restores already spent prevention.

For predictable handling without another prompt, consume active passive shields before revealed hand shields, in stable source order. Changes to passive shield strength affect future availability only. Champion damage and shield-use records reset after this attacking turn.
When the last Testudo dies, its permission to shield champions ends immediately after that attack. A later Testudo cannot replenish already-used allowances. Player shield protection remains separate.

An alternative shared army-wide shield pool is simpler to track but nerfs the current card substantially; fully refreshing shield amounts on every hit creates excessive repeat-hit prevention. The recommended separate allowances avoid both changes.

package_notes: Only the five catch-up proposals were reassessed. All other reviewed card changes, initial-shop rules, Crown timing and champion-combat proposals remain as in v3.
Seeker’s conditional mastery is 2. Riftbreaker costs 3 and gives 5 power. Courier costs 2 and heals 5 conditionally. Scout uses Warp 2. Aegis keeps its existing values.
Four of the five new cards cost 2 or less: Seeker, Courier, Aegis and Scout. Riftbreaker costs 3; it stays outside Warp 2, early Deadly Recruits and Conscription.
Scout can Warp another physical Scout, but selected cards leave the shop before effects. The two copies do not form a self-repeating loop.
Trigger-rate examples are assumptions for sensitivity analysis. Warp probabilities use uniform fresh stock and cannot be read as measured rates in strategic games.
Healing is capped normally, but Volos’s conversion effects can still reward requested healing at full health. Hand shield and ordinary healing values are tracked separately.
Mastery changes affect Giga, Order Initiate, Shard Seer, Omnius and Shard Abstractor together; measure M10/M20/M30 timing and every hero matchup after adaptation.
All five catch-up cards compare only mastery, strictly. Equal mastery gives no bonus; evaluate again at each effect resolution. They add two copies per faction, ten cards total.
Crown draws before its M20 Unify check, so its drawn card may supply a matching hand reveal. Its own mastery gain can reach M20.
Initial-shop filtering is setup-only. First-turn purchase and reroll refills can still reveal cards costing 6 or more.
Sequential champion removal changes live defense auras and shield sources; legality and costs must be recalculated after each resolved action.
The old statistics describe the pre-patch rules. The combined package needs new engine checks and adapted-policy evaluation before drawing balance conclusions.

design_reassessment.scope: Five mastery catch-up designs; all other card and combat proposals retained.
design_reassessment.method: Resource-by-resource comparisons, trigger-probability sensitivity, exact physical-copy Warp target calculations. No simulated win rates.
